Performers
David Wise (violin), Liverpool Philharmonic Orchestra (orchestra), Malcolm Sargent (conductor) Documented

Both sources name the three. The Archive description adds a presumption that Wise was the orchestra’s leader; that is not independently established here.

[1] [3]
Work version
Romance for violin and orchestra; the orchestral version made in 1920, first played in June 1921. Documented

The Internet Archive description and the Discogs label credit call it a Romance for violin and orchestra. The performing edition is not identified, and nothing in the item points to cuts across its four sides.

[1] [4] [5]
Recorded
1947-04-18 Documented

Both sources give 18 April 1947.

[1] [3]
Place
Philharmonic Hall, Liverpool Documented

Both sources name the hall.

[1] [3]
Label
English Columbia (Columbia Graphophone Co., Ltd.) Documented

Two 12-inch 78-rpm records.

[1] [3]
Catalogue
DX 1386–⁠1387 Documented

The Archive item gives September 1947 as the issue month. Discogs dates the UK set to 1947 and notes the “ST” tax code (April 1946 – November 1947).

[1] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Matrices CAX 9863 to 9866, all first takes (four sides) Documented

Stated in the Archive item’s description. The labels and stampers were not examined for this dossier.

[1]
Transfer
Internet Archive “Shellackophile” recordings collection Documented

The item is filed in that collection; no transfer engineer is named in the description.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Archive upload date (2 April 2022) is not a transfer date.

[1]
Processing
FLAC original with a variable-bitrate MP3 derivative, joined from four 78-rpm sides into one file. Documented

Equalisation, speed correction and noise reduction are not documented.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Vaughan Williams’s copyright in the music runs to the end of 2028 in the UK and EU. Documented

The Vaughan Williams Foundation gives 2028 as the year copyright in his music expires. Composition rights are separate from the recording.

[6]
Recording rights
Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial issue in 1947, before 1963 Inferred, not documented

The project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule applies to this 1947 Columbia set: its former 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is not United States or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.

[1] [3] [7]

Ralph Vaughan Williams, The Lark Ascending; David Wise, Liverpool Philharmonic Orchestra, Malcolm Sargent. English Columbia DX 1386–⁠1387 (1947), Internet Archive transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; Vaughan Williams’s copyright subsists in the UK and EU until the end of 2028.

Master release: https://www.discogs.com/master/3108264. Accessed 2026-10-18.
